newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Blues' face red after $145 mln loss.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Blues' face red after $145 mln loss.

text.p: A draft report released on Wednesday by the Massachusetts Insurance commissioner found that inept management caused a $145 million loss for the state's Blue Cross Blue Shield organization.

The examination, ordered by Insurance Commissioner Linda Ruthardt and done by Arthur Andersen found for 1996 operations a substantial net underwriting loss of $145 million, and a net loss of $90 million in the 1996 annual statement filed with the state agency.

The report recommends that a Division of Insurance representative should attend all meetings of the Blue Cross Board of Directors and any special committee meetings. It also recommends a the divsion have a representative on-site to monitor day-to-day transactions at the company.
Finally, the report recommends that the division or an appointed third party should perform periodic premium and claims testing in 1997.

"Blue Cross indicated to us even before the official presentation to them of the final language of the draft (report) that they wanted to work with the division to help assure that they not only remain a viable manager of health care and health insurance, but also to demonstrate" to officials and customers that it is taking appropriate steps to improve performance, Ruthhardt said.
Ruthardt said the losses were due to mismanagement.

"There is nothing here which is talking about grand fraud, corruption or malfeaseance. This is management." Ruthardt said. While she declined to call the company grossly mismanaged, Ruthardt did say "there are indications of incredible opportunities for change and improvement.
